add.title: Waves – Formation, Types and Wave Energy
add.md:
# Waves – Formation, Types and Wave Energy
- **How waves form:** **wind** blowing over the sea surface passes its **energy** to the water; waves are the **horizontal movement of energy**, not of water.
  - Wave size depends on **wind speed**, **duration** (how long it blows) and **fetch** (the open-water distance over which it blows) – the longer the fetch, the bigger the wave.
  - Largest waves form in the **open ocean**; strong westerlies of the **Southern Ocean ("Roaring Forties")** give some of the biggest swells.
- **Motion of water:** water particles move in **circular (orbital) paths** and come back almost to the same place; the motion fades with depth and is negligible below about **half the wavelength**.
- **Sea vs swell:** **sea** = steep, irregular waves still under the generating wind; **swell** = smooth, regular, long-period waves that have left the storm and travel thousands of km.
- **Breaking near the shore:** as water shallows the wave **slows, shortens and steepens**, the crest topples – a **breaker**; the foamy water rushing up the beach = **swash**, running back = **backwash**.
  - **Constructive waves** (low, gentle, strong swash) build beaches; **destructive waves** (high, steep, strong backwash) erode them – the basis of coastal landforms.
- **Wave refraction:** waves bend round headlands, so energy concentrates on **headlands (erosion)** and spreads in **bays (deposition)**.
- **Other wave-type hazards:**
  - **Tsunami** – seismic sea wave, not wind-made (see above).
  - **Storm surge** – a wind- and low-pressure-driven rise of sea level with a cyclone; the main killer on the AP–Odisha coast.
  - **Kallakkadal / swell surge** – sudden flooding of the Kerala coast by swells from distant **Southern Ocean** storms, with no local wind; **INCOIS** launched the **Swell Surge Forecast System (Feb 2020)** giving about a week's warning.
  - **Rogue (freak) waves** – unusually high single waves in the open sea.
- **Wave energy in India:** India's first wave-energy plant – a **150 kW oscillating water column (OWC)** pilot at **Vizhinjam (Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala), 1991**, built by **IIT Madras** under the Department of Ocean Development; output was low and it was **decommissioned in 2011**. IIT Madras–NIOT later tested the **Sindhuja-I** floating wave-energy device.
- **AP angle:** INCOIS (Hyderabad) issues **high-wave and swell alerts** for the AP coast; RTGS relays them to fishermen; storm surge, not tsunami, is AP's recurrent wave hazard.
> Exam angle: waves carry energy, not water; bigger waves need faster wind, longer duration and longer **fetch**; Kallakkadal is a swell surge, not a tsunami; Vizhinjam (1991) = first wave-energy plant.
~~ Sources: NCERT Fundamentals of Physical Geography ch.12; INCOIS products launch (Drishti IAS, 28 Feb 2020); Wikipedia – Wave power in India; OpenEI MHKDR (150 kW Indian Wave Energy Program); The Better India (IIT Madras–NIOT wave turbine)

add.title: Agro-based Industries – Meaning, India and AP Clusters
add.md:
# Agro-based Industries – Meaning and India
- **Agro-based industries** use farm, plantation, livestock or fishery produce as raw material: **cotton and jute textiles, sugar, vegetable oils, tea and coffee processing, rice and flour mills, dairy, food processing, tobacco, leather**.
  - Located near the **raw material** when it is perishable or loses weight (sugar, tea, mango pulp, fish), near the **market** when it does not (cotton textiles).
- **Food processing** = a **sunrise sector**; Ministry of **Food Processing Industries**; schemes – **PM Kisan SAMPADA (2017)**, **PMFME (2020, ODOP)**, **PLI for food processing**, **Operation Greens (TOP)**.
# Andhra Pradesh – Agro-based Clusters
- **Mango pulp – Chittoor:** with neighbouring **Krishnagiri (TN)** it forms India's main mango-pulp belt, processing **Totapuri** mangoes; the two districts supply the bulk of India's processed-mango exports (about 70% by recent trade reports).
- **Chilli – Guntur:** **Guntur Mirchi Yard** is called **Asia's largest dried red-chilli market**; Guntur chilli has a **GI tag**; drying, grading and chilli-powder units cluster here.
- **Tobacco – Guntur and Prakasam:** **Tobacco Board** (Tobacco Board Act 1975; in existence from **1 Jan 1976**) has its **HQ at Guntur**; Virginia FCV tobacco auction platforms and processing units (e.g. ITC at Chirala, Guntur).
- **Rice milling – Godavari and Krishna deltas:** the "rice bowl" districts host hundreds of rice mills; **Kakinada** port handles rice exports.
- **Aqua processing – coastal districts:** AP is India's leader in **farmed shrimp (Vannamei)**; peeling, freezing and export units around **Bhimavaram, Nellore, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam** make it a top **marine-export** State.
- **Oil palm and edible oil – West and East Godavari, Eluru:** AP leads in oil palm; crushing mills produce **crude palm oil**.
- **Others:** sugar (Godavari districts, Visakhapatnam, Chittoor), jute mills (north coastal AP), dairy (**Chittoor**), coir (Konaseema), cashew processing (**Palasa, Srikakulam**), turmeric (**Duggirala**, Guntur).
- **Mega Food Parks (operational):** **Srini (Chittoor)** and **Godavari Mega Aqua (West Godavari)**.
- **AP Food Processing Policy (4.0) 2024-29** (G.O. 71, Oct 2024): targets about **₹30,000 crore** investment, **3 lakh jobs**, **30,000 entrepreneurs**; food processing is a "sustenance" sector of Industrial Policy 4.0.
> Exam angle: Chittoor = mango pulp; Guntur = chilli yard + Tobacco Board HQ; Palasa = cashew; AP's Mega Food Parks = Srini and Godavari Mega Aqua.
~~ Sources: Tobacco Board (tobaccoboard.com); Krishi Jagran (mango pulp clusters); Wikipedia – Guntur chilli; The Week / Telangana Today (AP six policies, Oct 2024); AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25; app notes 3:103, 3:136, 4:59
